papers.title: MAS-Guard: Unified Guardrails from Individual Agents to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.abstract: Agentic AI extends large language models (LLMs) from generating responses to planning and executing complex workflows, substantially expanding their utility while exposing applications to unsafe actions, information leakage, and adversarial manipulation. Multi-agent systems further expand these capabilities through specialization and collaboration, but distributed authority, heterogeneous roles, and opaque or potentially compromised participants make safeguarding even more challenging. Existing defenses address important individual threats but provide fragmented coverage across local execution, system-level interactions, and enforcement mechanisms. We introduce MAS-Guard, a unified framework that closes this gap for safeguarding single- and multi-agent AI applications containing both instrumentable and opaque agents. Within instrumentable agents, the proposed local Agent Guardrail (A-Guard) layer applies task-specific experts to assess agentic events. At the system level, developer-owned Agent Charters and a Control Plane combine deterministic structural checks of routes, agent capabilities, and message formats with semantic assessments of roles and message content. These complementary layers enable enforcement through a shared set of interventions: allow, reflection, confirmation, and block. Evaluated across six benchmarks covering diverse single- and multi-agent scenarios with three agent LLMs from different providers, MAS-Guard reduces the overall attack success rate by 71.5-86.3% relative to unguarded agents, while meeting the utility reference criterion on benign tasks.
papers.llm_summary: MAS-Guard cung cấp guardrails thống nhất cho hệ thống agent đơn và đa LLM: lớp A-Guard cục bộ, Agent Charters + Control Plane kiểm tra cấu trúc/ngữ nghĩa, thực thi qua allow/reflection/confirmation/block.
papers.llm_reason: Cực kỳ liên quan cốt lõi agent/multi-agent safety (33/35), benchmark 6 tập (20/25), nội dung an toàn AI rất dễ làm content 30+ và các can thiệp 4 nível áp dụng ngay khi build agent.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Debate for Explainable Trading: Reasoning, Consensus, and Performance in Simulated Markets
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for financial decision-making, yet it remains unclear whether improvements in reasoning quality translate into better economic outcomes. We investigate this question using a multi-agent debate framework for portfolio allocation in historical market simulations, where specialized agents propose, critique, and revise investment decisions. Reasoning quality is evaluated across four dimensions: logical validity, evidential support, alternative consideration, and causal alignment, and compared with downstream financial performance. Across 210 controlled runs, aggregate reasoning quality shows no meaningful relationship with Sharpe ratio (r = 0.07, p = 0.29) or total return (r = 0.03, p = 0.70). Structured prompting increases measured reasoning quality from about 0.72 to 0.84 (+17.7%, Cohen's d about 2.0), but these gains do not consistently translate into higher returns. We identify sycophantic convergence as a central failure mode, where agents abandon independent positions during critique-revision cycles and converge toward similar allocations. A Jensen-Shannon divergence intervention that preserves disagreement improves Sharpe by +0.14 (p = 0.028) and Sortino by +0.25 (p = 0.026), while interventions enforcing stronger causal reasoning do not improve financial performance. Our results suggest that multi-agent debate is most valuable when it preserves independent informational signals rather than simply improving measured reasoning quality.
papers.llm_summary: Multi-agent debate cho portfolio allocation: reasoning quality không liên quan Sharpe/return, JSD intervention cải thiện Sharpe +0.14.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent debate + business decision (30+18), 210 runs có stats rõ (22), liên quan trực tiếp quyết định tài chính (16), insight sycophantic convergence & JSD actionable mạnh (16).

papers.title: Act on Your Behalf, Beyond Your Authorization: Benchmarking LLM Agent Authorization Alignment
papers.abstract: When an LLM agent acts on behalf of a user, it is expected to act within the authorization scope the user grants. Existing agent evaluations largely measure task completion or harmful consequences and can therefore overlook actions that violate this delegation without producing conventional safety or privacy harms. We introduce AuthorizationBench, a benchmark of authorization alignment grounded in documented real-world cases. A scalable construction pipeline produces 286 executable tasks spanning situational triggers, the presence or absence of direct harmful consequences, and ten application domains. We execute every task with four models at two reasoning-effort settings across three agent harnesses in an authorization-aware sandbox that keeps authorized and out-of-authorization paths executable and observable, yielding 6,864 trajectories. Agents act out of authorization in 19.2% of trajectories, with rates ranging from 10.5% to 26.6% across the 24 configurations. Task completion does not imply authorization. Increasing reasoning effort leaves the aggregate rate nearly unchanged, with effects varying across models. On controlled pairs, agents act out of authorization at similar rates with (17.9%) and without (20.8%) direct harmful consequences, and more often under benign pressures than malicious injections (23.5% versus 17.6%, p=0.002). Our results show that task capability, additional reasoning, and consequence-oriented safety evaluation do not by themselves ensure authorization alignment. Moreover, agents that consult the principal before completing a task exhibit lower rates of out-of-authorization behavior (14.0% versus 21.6%, p<0.001), pointing to a tension between agent autonomy and preserving users' decision authority that calls for further human-centered study. Dataset and code are available at https://github.com/PEACH-Research-Lab/AuthorizationBench .
papers.llm_summary: AuthorizationBench benchmark 286 task/6.864 trajectory cho thấy agent LLM hành động ngoài phạm vi được ủy quyền tới 19,2%, và việc tăng reasoning effort không giảm được tỷ lệ này.
papers.llm_reason: Rất thực tiễn (benchmark quy mô lớn từ case thực) và cực kỳ relevant business: ai dùng agent tự động đều cần kiểm soát phạm vi ủy quyền — insight 'task completion ≠ authorization' là content gold cho đối tượng 30+.

papers.title: A Small Model Asks Better: Fine-Tuning Query Clarification for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.abstract: Query clarification is essential for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems that face ambiguous user queries. We consider multi-turn grounded conversational scenarios where a user query is either ill-formed or ambiguous in the context of the prior dialog or, more interestingly, it may be well-formed but when posed against retrieved documents there are multiple relevant interpretations. The task is to recognize both such cases and then generate an appropriate clarification request to the user. We present ClariEdge, a new dataset of approximately 3,900 examples that include such ambiguous queries along with negative examples that do not require clarification. We also show that a lightweight fine-tuned LoRA achieves 96.6% classification accuracy and outperforms prompted baselines of many larger models on both classification and quality of clarification generation. Our study shows that hard negatives are an essential ingredient to separate out queries that are truly ambiguous from queries that may look ambiguous but are not (i.e., can be resolved from the context). The same LoRA achieves high performance in both pre-retrieval and post-retrieval scenarios; thus, it can be used in two places in a RAG pipeline as a check before answer generation. The ClariEdge dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/ibm-research/ClariEdge.
papers.llm_summary: ClariEdge là dataset + pipeline fine-tune LoRA model nhỏ để RAG nhận diện truy vấn mơ hồ và hỏi làm rõ, đạt 96.6% accuracy, đánh bại các model lớn hơn.
papers.llm_reason: Ứng dụng trực tiếp cho chatbot/RAG của content creator: model nhỏ, dataset công khai, hard negatives, dùng được cả pre- và post-retrieval — đọc xong làm được ngay.

papers.title: Reasoning-Search-Augmented LLMs: An Operational Taxonomy, Benchmark Analysis and Controlled Evidence Synthesis
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive emergent reasoning capabilities, yet they remain constrained by fixed model parameters and finite context windows. Even when augmented with static retrieval, they can produce statements that are unsupported by, or even contradictory to, retrieved evidence. This leads to hallucinations, difficulty incorporating up-to-date information, and failures to correctly interpret or reconcile sources. Recent work addresses these limitations by tightly coupling step-by-step reasoning with interactive search, treating retrieval as an action within an iterative agentic loop rather than a one-shot preprocessing step. This study reviews frameworks that implement such reasoning-search loops by interleaving planning, querying, retrieval, integration, verification, and stopping. We analyze these systems through four architectural axes: retrieval coupling, controller design, knowledge source, and grounding strictness. We separately treat the learning signal as a cross-cutting dimension because prompting, supervision, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning can instantiate the same architecture while producing materially different search, stopping, and grounding behavior. We further distinguish benchmark difficulty from RSA-loop demand and synthesize controlled within-study ablations and quality-cost deltas, avoiding invalid pooling across heterogeneous model backbones, retrievers, corpora, and evaluation protocols. Our goal is to clarify the landscape of reasoning-search-augmented LLMs and outline a unified perspective on the design choices shaping future research.
papers.llm_summary: Tổng quan hệ thống LLM kết hợp suy luận và tìm kiếm tương tác theo vòng lặp agent, phân loại kiến trúc và tổng hợp bằng chứng kiểm soát.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan đến AI agent có khả năng tìm kiếm và suy luận, có benchmark và bằng chứng thực nghiệm, hữu ích cho nghiên cứu thị trường và sáng tạo nội dung chính xác.

papers.title: Write Once, Query Many: Evolving Compact Reusable Memory for Long Videos
papers.abstract: Long videos often exceed the context capacity of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), while agentic search repeats costly video processing and grounding for each query. Reusable memory can amortize this cost, but must preserve information for questions unknown during construction. We propose Video-EMem, an evolvable video memory harness built on time-anchored perceptual observations. This representation combines compact free-form text with sparse images to preserve semantic content and complementary visual details across temporal scales, supporting temporal navigation without a fixed semantic schema. A Writer encodes each video once by consolidating overlapping multiscale observations, and a Reader retrieves and organizes evidence solely from the resulting memory. With the underlying models frozen, we evolve their workflows and operators using distinct feedback: query-independent source fidelity and coverage for the Writer, and QA failures in evidence localization and utilization for the Reader. Experiments support this separation for generalization beyond development queries, with our evolution strategy improving average accuracy by 7.2% over the unevolved harness. While reducing storage by about 99.86% on average relative to raw videos, Video-EMem improves Qwen3-VL-30B by an average of 2.6% across three long-video QA benchmarks over direct input of 2,048 frames. Using the same o3 answer model as the state-of-the-art agentic method, it improves average accuracy by 2.5% with lower per-query latency.
papers.llm_summary: Video-EMem xây dựng bộ nhớ video tái sử dụng dạng compact cho MLLM, giảm 99.86% dung lượng và cải thiện QA video dài.
papers.llm_reason: Rất thực tiễn cho content video, có benchmark thật, pattern Writer-Reader reusable memory dễ áp dụng cho multi-channel.

papers.title: Context-Aware Prompt Injection Detection via Small Language Models in RAG Pipelines: nokast-secureRAG
papers.abstract: Local Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection and retrieval poisoning, where malicious instructions in retrieved content are mistaken for trusted input. We present nokast-secureRAG, a roughly 0.5B-parameter small language model that acts as a semantic firewall between retrieval and generation. It jointly evaluates the user query and retrieved context, classifying the pair as safe, suspicious, or malicious. The model is trained using a teacher-judge-student pipeline: a 35B teacher generates 5,233 examples across four attack families, and an independent 120B judge re-labels them, achieving 95.0% agreement before student fine-tuning. On a held-out in-distribution test set, the model achieves 0.994 detection recall at a 0.026 false-positive rate and a 0.006 attack-success-rate proxy, outperforming a regex baseline, a public prompt-injection classifier, Llama Guard 3 1B, and its untuned version. Prompt-Guard-86M reaches 0.900 recall but has a 0.690 false-positive rate. On a judgment-flip test, where the same sentence is benign or malicious depending on context, the model correctly classifies both cases 75% of the time, outperforming the compared baselines. Ablations indicate that retrieved context carries the main attack signal, while query-context consistency reduces false positives. Single-request latency is 293-404 ms, above the target of 100 ms, while amortized throughput latency is 37 ms under batching. On the external PoisonedRAG benchmark, recall falls to near zero, indicating that fluent fact-poisoning attacks lie outside the detector's instruction-consistency threat model. We report this limitation alongside the in-distribution results. The model, data-generation pipeline, and evaluation harness are released open source.
papers.llm_summary: nokast-secureRAG dùng SLM ~0,5B làm 'tường lửa ngữ nghĩa' giữa retrieval và generation trong RAG, đạt recall 0,994 ở FPR 0,026, latency 293–404ms.
papers.llm_reason: Thiết thực cao cho ai chạy RAG local (phát hiện prompt injection/poisoning với model nhỏ, metric rõ ràng), insight 'context mới là nơi chứa attack signal' rất actionable cho product và content bảo mật.

papers.title: Agentic Orchestration of EDC Data Space Retrieval and Natural Language Driven Data Processing
papers.abstract: Participating in a data space still requires the Dataspace Protocol (DSP) negotiation flow to be hand-coded against each provider's access policy. We present a multi-agent architecture that automates this process using natural language requests. Built on LangGraph over an Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC), the design separates concerns into cooperating agents. The orchestrator's role is to route and plan. The data extraction agent's role is to expose the DSP protocol's three composable tools (catalog discovery, contract negotiation and download). The agent also gates negotiations on the consumers' verifiable credentials, refusing assets rather than fabricating them. Furthermore, there are downstream Machine Learning (ML) and Visualization agents, as well as a final Verification agent, which confirms that the request was actually fulfilled and rechecks the intended operation against the contract's usage policy. In a primary benchmark involving 600 runs, the system achieved 89% task success with zero policy violations when evaluating multi-dimensional policy reasoning with a locally hosted open-weight model. It failed safely through refusal rather than misrouting. The reliability of the system is largely dependent on the phrasing of requests: technical and expert requests succeed up to 98% of the time, whereas casual and under-specified requests succeed 72% of the time. Furthermore, in a secondary evaluation of 600 runs isolating hierarchical geographic access control, the framework successfully blocks 100% of unauthorized regional requests. While the verification agent hallucinates that 1% of these requests, the system logs confirm that no data is ever extracted and the framework simultaneously achieves an end-to-end verified delivery rate of 86% for eligible consumers.
papers.llm_summary: Kiến trúc multi-agent trên LangGraph tự động hóa đàm phán Dataspace Protocol bằng ngôn ngữ tự nhiên (orchestrator + extraction + ML/visualization + verification agents), đạt 89% success, 0 vi phạm policy.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent orchestration rõ ràng (30/35), benchmark 600 runs thật (22/25), insight về phân tách vai trò và tác động của cách diễn đạt request (98% vs 72%) rất actionable cho content về prompting.

papers.title: Editing as Language: Teaching LLM Agents a Grammar for Native Context Editing
papers.abstract: A synopsis in novels folds a story into a few lines; a function in code gathers many steps with a single execution. Context editing is native to language itself. In this paper, we propose the Native Context Editing (NCE) framework, which gives language model agents a grammar for natively editing their own context. By encoding context-editing operations in a grammar of dedicated special tokens, we teach the agents to invoke edits through the language itself. We train agents on iteratively constructed trajectory segments, with each teacher edit conditioned on the evolving context. This establishes context editing as an atomic and inherent capability of LLM agents, enabling them to dynamically modify their context as they generate responses over long-horizon reasoning and interaction. Compared with context-editing methods that learn to generate tool-use code within specific external harness environments, our approach integrates context editing as an internal mechanism of the model's native generation process, enabling better generalization across diverse real-world workflows. On four long-horizon agentic benchmarks (Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Multilingual, and SWE-bench Pro), NCE improves the average task success rate over the base model by 5.6 percentage points for LongCat-Flash-Lite-Sparse and by 4.5 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, while reducing average token usage by 36% and 15%, respectively.
papers.llm_summary: NCE dạy agent LLM ngữ pháp chỉnh sửa context bằng special tokens, cải thiện +5.6pp trên 4 benchmark long-horizon (Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench) và giảm token.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan agent/context/tool-use, benchmark thật, insight về context editing và hiệu quả token áp dụng được cho workflow content automation.

papers.title: BetaMem: Learning to Remember a Changing World for Embodied Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon embodied agents face temporal confusion and incomplete or distorted records, recurring errors from fixed memory rules, and growing storage and retrieval costs. We present BetaMem, a framework for building and evolving traceable long-term memory through six linked layers: working, spatial, entity, episodic, experiential, and procedural memory. A dual-level write contract constrains operation executability and source support for content: supervised fine-tuning learns compliant memory operations, while reinforcement learning combines repeated sampling with teacher verification of the original observations to reward complete, accurate records and penalize omissions, distortion, and unsupported content. We formulate failure-driven policy recursive self-improvement through diagnosis along the causal sequence of memory operations and local rule repairs gated by independent replay. Atomic tools frame storage, updates, retrieval, and forgetting as cost-utility allocation under storage and read budgets. Using the open-source Qwen3.5-9B model for memory generation, BetaMem achieves overall scores of 48.08% on M3-Bench-robot, 92.08% on LoCoMo, 72.6% on OpenEQA EM-EQA, and 62.4% on EgoLifeQA, the highest among the listed memory methods under their respective evaluation protocols. Training the model for memory generation raises the contract pass rate from 50.9% to 86.2% while reducing output tokens per stored action by 47.3%. A separate Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct evaluation on EMem-Bench achieves an average success rate of 38.4% and an average error recurrence rate of 24.9%. We perform best among evaluated methods using comparably sized open-source models. Category results show that we have advantages in integrating information across observations, recalling events over long histories, and inferring personal habits.
papers.llm_summary: BetaMem xây dựng bộ nhớ dài hạn 6 lớp (làm việc, không gian, thực thể, sự kiện, kinh nghiệm, thủ tục) cho agent embodied, dùng SFT+RL để ghi/chỉnh sửa bộ nhớ đúng quy tắc và tiết kiệm chi phí lưu trữ.
papers.llm_reason: Cực kỳ sát lõi agent/tool-use với benchmark thật (LoCoMo 92%, M3-Bench...), nhưng thiênên về embodied nên ít áp dụng trực tiếp vào content/business, trừ khi làm sản phẩm agent cần nhớ ngữ cảnh dài.
